item.title: Lifts of symmetries to minimal nondegenerate extensions are unique up to fermion attachment
item.description: arXiv:2610.14847v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Gauging fermion parity in a $(2+1)$-dimensional fermionic topological order requires lifting its symmetries to the resulting bosonic theory. We give a direct tensor-categorical proof that, for a slightly degenerate braided fusion category $\mathcal{C}$ and a fixed minimal nondegenerate extension ${\cal E}$, the restriction homomorphism $r\colon\operatorname{Aut}_{\mathrm{LR}}(\mathcal{E})\to \operatorname{Aut}_{\mathrm{LR}}(\mathcal{C})$ on classes of complex-linear locality-respecting (LR) braided autoequivalences is surjective with central kernel $\mathbb{Z}/2$, generated by fermion attachment. Thus each symmetry class has exactly two LR lift classes, related by attaching the fermion to every vortex. We apply graded Morita theory to reduce the kernel to two module types on the vortex sector, corresponding to tensoring with the vacuum or the fermion. We then prove relative rigidity to show that each type determines a unique LR class, which are distinguished by fermionic self-braiding even when their actions on simple-object labels coincide. We prove surjectivity by extending graph algebras in $\mathcal{C}^{\mathrm{rev}}\boxtimes\mathcal{C}$ to Lagrangian algebras in $\mathcal{E}^{\mathrm{rev}}\boxtimes\mathcal{E}$. Our results require neither unitarity nor a ribbon structure. We illustrate the lifting ambiguity in the Laughlin state, the $SO(3)_3$ theory and the Ising topological order.
item.dc:creator: Ran Luo, Jiahua Tian

item.title: Quantum Pick's Theorem in two dimensions
item.description: arXiv:2610.15234v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Consider an $n$-dimensional sum of the form $S_k=\sum{q^{f({\bf z})}}$ over lattice points ${\bf z}$ which lie in $K{\mathcal P}$, the $K$ scaling of an $n$-dimensional rational polytope $\mathcal P$. We formulate a conjecture on the structure of $S_K$ considered for $K$ prime, as a power series in $h=q-1$ modulo the $K^{th}$ cyclotomic polynomial, and in particular the existence of a decomposition in powers of the Gauss sum $\mathbb G$, up to the $n^{th}$, whose coefficients are almost independent of $K$, where the leading coefficient is related to the volume of $\mathcal P$ and the coefficient of ${\mathbb G}^r$ has contributions from the codimension $r$ skeleton of $\mathcal P$. The conjecture is proved for $n=1,2$.
item.dc:creator: Moris Metin Bardavid, Ruth Lawrence

item.title: Type $B$- and $C$- trigonometric weight functions
item.description: arXiv:2610.15344v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce and study trigonometric weight functions of type $B$ and type $C$ arising from integrable lattice models. These functions give $q$-deformations of the factorial $K$-theoretic Schur $P$- and $Q$-functions of Ikeda and Naruse, with the $P$-functions specialized to the type $B$ case. We realize them as specializations of partition functions of a six-vertex model with triangular boundary conditions and derive their algebraic properties using the Yang-Baxter equation and properties of the $R$- and $K$-matrices. We introduce normalized weight functions and establish diagonal evaluation formulas, divisibility properties, and bounds on Newton polytopes analogous to those in type $A$, together with recursive relations and stability. We further derive branching formulas relating these functions to type $A$ weight functions, and prove equal-cardinality orthogonality and all-cardinality biorthogonality relations.
item.dc:creator: Kohei Motegi

item.title: The First Modular Zhu Algebra of $L(\frac12,0)_F$ in Characteristic Seven
item.description: arXiv:2610.15448v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $F$ be an algebraically closed field of characteristic $7$, and let $V=L(\frac12,0)_F$. For the degree-four singular vector $q=(L(-2)^2-2L(-4))\mathbf1$ in the universal vacuum vertex operator algebra $\bar V$, set $V_q=\bar V/I(q)$. We prove that the natural quotient map induces an isomorphism $A_1(V_q)\cong A_1(V)\cong F[T]/(T(T-4)(T-5))\cong F^3$. Explicit $O_1(V_q)$-relations and four families of triangular PBW straightening relations give the upper bound, while three one-dimensional homogeneous subspaces give the matching lower bound.
item.dc:creator: Haihua Huang

item.title: The Deligne--Drinfeld conjecture after OpenAI
item.description: arXiv:2610.15592v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We provide a simplified and more human-friendly version of the proof of the Deligne--Drinfeld conjecture recently given by OpenAI. No originality is claimed.
item.dc:creator: Thomas Willwacher

item.title: A trace lower bound for totally positive units in $\mathbb{Q}(\zeta_p)^+$ and its application to fusion category
item.description: arXiv:2610.15643v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $p = 4q + 1$ be a prime integer, where $q$ is an odd prime. Let $L = \mathbb{Q}(\zeta_p)^+$ denote the maximal totally real subfield of the $p$-th cyclotomic field $\mathbb{Q}(\zeta_p)$. In this paper, we prove that if $U_L^+=U_L^2$ (i.e., every totally positive unit is a square in $L$), then for any non-trivial subfield $K \subseteq L$ and any non-trivial totally positive unit $\varepsilon \in U_K^+$, the absolute trace satisfies the sharp lower bound $\Tr_{K/\mathbb{Q}}(\varepsilon) \ge p - 4$. As an application, we show that a spherical fusion category $\C$ with global dimension $\dim(\mathcal{C})=p=4q+1$ is pointed, where $2$ is a primitive root modulo $q$, or $p=4q+1<2^{22}$ and $p\neq 29$.
item.dc:creator: Yue Meng, Zhiqiang Yu

item.title: A Multiplicative Horn Obstruction to the Unitary Categorification of a Rank-Twelve Modular Datum
item.description: arXiv:2610.15792v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the rank-twelve potential modular datum denoted $12^{39,406}_{4,1276.}$ in the low-rank classification tables. Its global dimension is $(1287+351\sqrt{13})/2$, and its fusion ring agrees with that of the known rank-twelve Haagerup modular category. The datum satisfies the modular relations, has nonnegative integral Verlinde coefficients, and passes several familiar genus-one necessary tests. We prove, nevertheless, that it cannot be realized by a unitary modular tensor category. The obstruction already occurs in the representation of the three-strand braid group on $\operatorname{Hom}(C_{[10]},B^{\otimes3})$. Generalized Frobenius--Schur indicators determine the eigenvalues of the two-strand generator on this twelve-dimensional space. The central relation in $B_3$ then reduces the problem to a product of three prescribed unitary conjugacy classes. A sixfold symmetry reduces the $1302$ determinant-compatible cases to $217$ representatives. Rank-one inequalities leave only $17$ of these, and ten explicitly displayed degree-zero rank-two Schubert inequalities exclude the remaining cases. A violated inequality with gap $2/117$ is worked out explicitly. All calculations used in the obstruction are exact. The argument uses unitarity essentially and leaves non-unitary categorification open.
item.dc:creator: Jiuhe Liu, Xuzhihan Ding

item.title: Derivation based noncommutative geometry of quiver path algebras
item.description: arXiv:2610.16300v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we study derivation based noncommutative geometry of path algebras arising from quivers by identifying a Lie algebra of derivations from which a differential calculus is constructed. We show that properties of the differential calculus are intimately connected with the structure of the quiver. In particular, by introducing the notion of a separating quiver, we find a condition on the quiver which is equivalent to the module of differential forms being a projective bimodule. For such quivers, one can construct bimodule connections, as well as bimodule forms which serve as noncommutative analogues of the Riemannian metric. As an illustration of the above concepts, we present a class of quivers for which one can construct Levi-Civita connections, i.e. torsion free connections compatible with a bimodule form.
item.dc:creator: Joakim Arnlind, Victor Hildebrandsson

item.title: On the Drinfeld doubles of Laistrygonian algebras in positive characteristic
item.description: arXiv:2610.16665v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this work, we study restricted Laistrygonian algebras over a field of positive characteristic $p$. We compute their Drinfeld double $\mathtt{D_p(q,a)}$ and give explicit presentations by generators and relations. We prove that $\mathtt{D_p(q,a)}$ is a pointed Hopf algebra. For $\mathtt{D_p(1,a)}$, we describe an abelian exact sequence of Hopf algebras and identify one of its quotients as a restricted enveloping Lie algebra. This exact sequence enables us to classify the finite-dimensional simple $\mathtt{D_p(1,a)}$-modules. We also introduce an infinite-dimensional Hopf algebra covering the restricted Drinfeld double and study its relation with the corresponding finite-dimensional case. Using this covering together with a Frobenius map, we construct a $3\times 3$ commutative diagram whose rows and columns are exact sequences of Hopf algebras. In particular, our approach provides a unified treatment of the Drinfeld doubles associated with restricted Laistrygonian algebras in arbitrary positive characteristic.
item.dc:creator: Nicol\'as Andruskiewitsch, Dirceu Bagio, Saradia Della Flora, Daiana Flores, Oscar M\'arquez, H\'ector Mart\'in Pe\~na Pollastri

item.title: Cyclic reflections and the flip equation for the graded Grothendieck-Teichm\"uller group
item.description: arXiv:2610.17482v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Furusho, Hirose and Komiyama reformulated the pentagon equation using an involution called the flip, which led to a new characterisation of the graded Grothendieck-Teichm\"uller group $\mathsf{GRT}_1$. We show that the flip is a reflection in the cyclic structure of the operad of framed Drinfeld-Kohno Lie algebras, with the framings removed. Applying the reflection twice to the pentagon gives the two-cycle relation for every Drinfeld associator. This relation is precisely the condition for cyclic compatibility on the associativity morphism, giving a new proof that $\mathsf{GRT}_1$ acts by cyclic automorphisms of parenthesized ribbon chord diagrams.
item.dc:creator: Chandan Singh

item.title: On quasi-lisse affine vertex algebras $L_{-1-h/6}(\mathfrak{g})$ from rank-one Argyres-Douglas theories
item.description: arXiv:2610.17676v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study certain simple affine vertex algebras $L_{-1-h/6}(\mathfrak{g})$ from rank-one Argyres-Douglas theories, where $\mathfrak{g}$ is a non-simply-laced simple Lie algebra and $h$ is its Coxeter number. For $L_{-3}(F_4)$, we determine the maximal ideal of $V^{-3}(F_4)$, Zhu's algebra, and the associated variety. We also classify the irreducible highest-weight $L_{-3}(F_4)$-modules and determine the characters of its irreducible ordinary modules. The associated variety is $\overline{\mathbb{O}}_{\widetilde A_1}$, and the level $-3$ is totally collapsing for the orbit $\mathbb{O}_{\widetilde A_1}$. The Poisson coinvariants of the $C_2$-algebra of $L_{-3}(F_4)$ are isomorphic to $\mathbb{C}[\ell]/(\ell^5)$, where $\ell$ is induced by the conformal vector. Consequently, the characters of ordinary $L_{-3}(F_4)$-modules satisfy a fifth-order modular linear differential equation. We also give modular linear differential equations of orders five and eleven satisfied by the characters of ordinary modules for $L_{-2}(B_3)$ and $L_{-2}(G_2)$ respectively.
item.dc:creator: Drazen Adamovic, Xuanzhong Dai, Kaiwen Sun

item.title: Quandles with isomorphic representation categories
item.description: arXiv:2610.17769v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We give two types of examples where two non isomorphic finite quandles have isomorphic enveloping groups. This implies that two non-isomorphic finite quandles can share isomorphic representation categories (as additive and tensor categories simultaneously).
item.dc:creator: Mohamad Maassarani

item.title: Cellular Algebra of $A_2$ webs
item.description: arXiv:2610.18801v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce a diagram algebra $\mathcal{K}_L$ based on Kuperberg's $A_2$-webs and prove a Schur--Weyl duality $\mathcal{K}_L \cong \operatorname{End}_{U_q(\mathfrak{sl}_3)}((V^+ \oplus V^-)^{\otimes L})$, where $V^\pm$ are the fundamental representations of $U_q(\mathfrak{sl}_3)$. Thus, $\mathcal{K}_L$ is a natural $A_2$ analogue of the Temperley--Lieb algebra. We construct an explicit cellular structure for $\mathcal{K}_L$, with the web basis as its cellular basis and cell modules indexed by dominant $U_q(\mathfrak{sl}_3)$-weights. The bases of these modules are parametrized by dominant lattice paths via a recursive growth algorithm. Using this structure, we determine local generators of $\mathcal{K}_L$ and establish web formulations of the first and second fundamental theorems of invariant theory. In particular, we show that the braid-group image, augmented by local idempotents, does not generate $\mathcal{K}_L$, and identify an additional local generator. Finally, we derive a bimodule decomposition of $(V^+ \oplus V^-)^{\otimes L}$, yielding a complete set of irreducible $\mathcal{K}_L$-modules for formal or generic $q$.
item.dc:creator: Azat M. Gainutdinov, Jesper Lykke Jacobsen, Yueheng Li

item.title: Haagerup conformal field theory at central charge eight
item.description: arXiv:2610.14441v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We construct a chiral algebra $U$ of central charge eight inside the lattice vertex operator algebra $V_{E_6\oplus A_2}$. It is generated by two commuting affine $\mathfrak{sl}_2$ current algebras at levels $1$ and $39$, the stress tensor of the lattice theory, and a single weight-two field built from three lattice exponentials. We announce that $U$ is strongly rational and completely unitary, and that $Rep(U)$ is equivalent, as a unitary ribbon category, to the Drinfeld center $Z(\mathcal{H}_3)$ of the Haagerup fusion category $\mathcal{H}_3$. Its characters are the $\gamma=0$ Evans--Gannon vector. From $U$ we obtain a diagonal full CFT, and also a holomorphic $E_8$ extension on which $\mathcal{H}_3$ acts by topological defects.
item.dc:creator: Tzu-Chen Huang

item.title: A categorical approach to the set-theoretic Yang-Baxter equation
item.description: arXiv:2610.15347v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We investigate set-theoretic solutions of the Yang--Baxter equation from a categorical perspective. The paper has two main objectives. On the one hand, several existing constructions and classification results in the literature are recast in categorical terms, thereby showing that certain hypotheses previously imposed on such solutions are in fact superfluous. On the other hand, the categorical approach leads naturally to new classes of Yang-Baxter solutions. Our approach consists in identifying suitable subcategories of the category $\mathcal{YB}$ of Yang-Baxter solutions and providing categorical characterisations of the solutions they encode. As an application, we prove that the category of P{\l}onka bi-magmas is isomorphic to the subcategory of $\mathcal{YB}$ consisting of solutions of the Baaj-Long-Skandalis equation. Along the way, we introduce and study a new class of Lyubashenko type solutions and examine the extent to which non-degenerate bijective solutions of the braid equation arise from skew left braces.
item.dc:creator: A. L. Agore, A. Chirvasitu, G. Militaru

item.title: Bimodule duality and Artin's problem for skew field extensions
item.description: arXiv:2610.15469v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Emil Artin asked whether the left and right dimensions of an extension of skew fields must agree. Cohn and Schofield gave counterexamples through elaborate constructions. It has been a long-standing open question whether there is any division ring, infinite-dimensional over its center, for which the left and right indices agree whenever at least one is finite. We give the first such examples. Call a division ring index-symmetric if every division subring with at least one finite index has equal finite indices. Using a duality formula for bimodules over division algebras, we prove that every twisted Calabi--Yau division algebra is index-symmetric. The examples include the Weyl skew fields and, more generally, the quotient division rings of rings of differential operators on smooth affine varieties in characteristic zero. Further examples are the quotient division rings of enveloping algebras of finite-dimensional Lie algebras, Ore extensions of twisted Calabi--Yau noetherian domains, quantum affine spaces, and group algebras of torsion-free polycyclic-by-finite groups.
item.dc:creator: Niels Lauritzen, Jesper Funch Thomsen

item.title: A noetherian Hopf algebra has bijective antipode
item.description: arXiv:2610.15473v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove that a Hopf algebra over an arbitrary field has a bijective antipode if either its left or right regular module has finite uniform dimension. In particular, this solves Skryabin's conjecture, posed in 2006, that every noetherian Hopf algebra has a bijective antipode. Starting from Skryabin's injectivity theorem for weakly finite Hopf algebras, we associate to each finite-dimensional subcoalgebra an essential left ideal of common denominators that is also a right coideal in the antipode image. An annihilator identity makes this image essential in the original algebra as a left module over the image, yielding finite left uniform dimension from finite right uniform dimension. A second denominator construction inside the antipode image, together with a restricted inverse-antipode identity, proves surjectivity.
item.dc:creator: Andrea Sciandra

item.title: Monoidal structure on Rota-Baxter algebras via augmentation, and free cocycle bialgebras
item.description: arXiv:2610.17525v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A tensor product is known for commutative Rota--Baxter algebras through a universal construction, but its underlying algebra need not be the ordinary tensor product $A\otimes B$ and can be substantially larger. We show that, after passing to augmented Rota--Baxter algebras, the ordinary tensor product itself carries a natural Rota--Baxter operator which makes the category monoidal with the usual associator and unit constraints. The resulting structure is intrinsically nonsymmetric: over a field of characteristic zero, this operator and its flip-conjugated counterpart are the only possibilities among linear combinations of five natural terms, while over any field the full category admits no braiding. Its comonoid objects are precisely Rota--Baxter cocycle bialgebras. Moreover, the free Rota--Baxter adjunction yields a bimonad and free cocycle bialgebras on ordinary bialgebras, with compatible Hopf structures for connected filtered inputs, in both the associative and commutative settings.
item.dc:creator: Li Guo, Yunzhou Xie, Yi Zhang

item.title: A subcategory with remarkable homological properties via actions of tensor categories
item.description: arXiv:2610.17646v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: By equipping the category $\mathcal{M}$ of modules over a finite dimensional algebra with the action of a finite tensor category $\mathcal{C}$, we introduce a subcategory $\mathcal{PM}$ satisfying numerous remarkable properties: it is generating and cogenerating, functorially finite, closed under Auslander--Reiten translations (i.e. precluster tilting), and it computes the finitistic dimension. Through a functor category perspective, $\mathcal{PM}$ is identified with the $\mathcal{C}$-module functors that are projective, and we also prove a $\mathcal{C}$-equivariant version of the Auslander(--Solberg) correspondence. As examples, we show that $\mathcal{PM}$ contains only finitely many indecomposable modules for some tensor product algebras. For some family of 1-Iwanaga--Gorenstein algebras introduced by Geiss--Leclerc--Schr\"oer, we show that $\mathcal{PM}$ is exactly the subcategory of $\tau$-locally free modules.
item.dc:creator: Kevin Coulembier, Edmund Heng

item.title: Haagerup-Izumi modular data from hyperbolic words: S-fold TQFTs, central charge, torsion and the Bethe vacua
item.description: arXiv:2610.18512v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The modular data of the doubles of the Haagerup--Izumi categories is a grafting of two finite metric groups (conjectured by Evans--Gannon, proved for untwisted categories by Gannon--Schopieray--Yadav). Gang and Kim found non-unitary modular data of this shape in the topological twist of rank-$0$ $S$-fold theories, from the Bethe vacua of an abelianised gauge theory. The aim is to understand rigorously the significance of the handle-gluing and fibering operators, and to construct the Bethe vacua. For every hyperbolic once-punctured-torus monodromy $\varphi$, a word in $L$ and $R$, the two groups are $A_\mp=\coker(\varphi\mp1)$, with the torsion linking forms of the mapping tori of $\varphi$ and $-\varphi$. Over all words of trace $m^2+2$ these forms reproduce the Evans--Gannon table of Q-systems, one printed entry being corrected, and the distinct modular data in the list of Gannon--Schopieray--Yadav. The Bethe data are given in closed form by the word: the level matrix, the positive vacuum, $c_{\eff}=\#L$, and the handle-gluing values $2^{\#L}\lambda^{\pm1}|A_-||A_+|$ at the identity classes, $\lambda$ the stretch factor. Each kernel vector of $\varphi\mp1$ modulo $|A_\mp|$ at which an explicit trigonometric formula does not vanish gives a solution of the Bethe equations in closed form. Under the half-index dictionary, with the unit in the class of $\sigma V^*$, $c\equiv\#L-6\#R\pmod{24}$.
item.dc:creator: David E Evans

item.title: A proof of the framed LMOV conjecture for links
item.description: arXiv:2610.18618v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove the Labastida--Mari\~no--Ooguri--Vafa conjecture for oriented links with arbitrary integer framings. Consequently, the framed reformulated invariants have finite integral LMOV expansions for every integer framing vector.
item.dc:creator: Kefeng Liu, Pan Peng, Shengmao Zhu

item.title: On finite dimensionality of homology of subalgebras of vector fields
item.description: arXiv:2211.08510v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We show that finite tensor products of modules of tensor fields are Noetherian modules over any graded Lie subalgebra of finite codimension in the Lie algebra of polynomial vector fields on $\mathbb{R}^n$. As a corollary, we prove the conjecture of I.\,M. Gelfand, announced at the ICM in Nice in 1970, on the finite-dimensionality of the continuous cohomology of graded Lie subalgebras of finite codimension in the Lie algebra of formal vector fields $\mathcal{W}_n$. We also prove that tensor products of modules of densities are Noetherian over the Witt Lie algebra of polynomial vector fields on the punctured line. Moreover, for a weight $\lambda\neq0,1$ every nonzero submodule of the symmetric power $S^r(\mathcal{T}_\lambda)$ contains $\Delta^{2N}S^r(\mathcal{T}_\lambda)$, where $\Delta$ is the Vandermonde determinant. As a consequence, we show that a conjecture of Etingof implies the conjecture of Petukhov and Sierra on the simplicity of the quotients $U({\mathfrak{vir}})/(C-c)$ of the enveloping algebra of the Virasoro algebra.
item.dc:creator: Boris Feigin, Alexei Kanel-Belov, Anton Khoroshkin

item.title: P{\l}onka bi-magmas and the set-theoretic Yang--Baxter equation
item.description: arXiv:2305.14138v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We introduce a new variety of universal algebras with two binary operations, called \emph{P{\l}onka bi-magmas}, and use them to construct novel solutions to the set-theoretic Yang-Baxter (YB) equation. We establish explicit structural and classification results for P{\l}onka bi-magmas, which allow for a detailed study of the induced families of YB-solutions. In particular, we identify and classify several naturally arising classes of YB-solutions from the universal algebra perspective, including the so-called bi-connected and ideal-simple ones. For instance, we prove that there are only countably many isomorphism classes of induced YB-solutions which are ideal-simple, and characterize them in terms of the odometer transformations familiar from ergodic theory. In particular, if $X$ is a finite set with $|X| = n$, then the number of isomorphism classes of all the induced ideal-simple YB-solutions on $X$ is equal to the sum of all divisors of $n$.
item.dc:creator: A. L. Agore, A. Chirvasitu, G. Militaru

item.title: Partially compactified quantum cluster structures on simple algebraic groups and the full Berenstein--Zelevinsky conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2504.05134v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The construction of partially compactified cluster algebras on coordinate rings is handled by using codimension 2 arguments on cluster covers. An analog of this in the quantum situation is highly desirable but has not been found yet. In this paper, we present a general method for the construction of partially compactified quantum cluster algebra structures on quantized coordinate rings from that of quantum cluster algebra structures on localizations. As an application, we construct a partially compactified quantum cluster algebra structure on the quantized coordinate ring of every connected, simply connected complex simple algebraic group. Along the way, we settle in full the Berenstein--Zelevinsky conjecture that all quantum double Bruhat cells have quantum cluster algebra structures associated to seeds indexed by arbitrary signed words, and prove that all such seeds are linked to each by mutations.
item.dc:creator: Fan Qin, Milen Yakimov

item.title: Trace-function frames and modularity of genus-one conformal blocks
item.description: arXiv:2508.01294v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The recursive relations and modular transformation laws of trace functions have a common geometric source: conformal blocks on pointed elliptic curves. For a simple, rational, $C_2$-cofinite, CFT-type vertex operator algebra and an irreducible module $W$ of it, we identify the bundle $\mathscr{C}_{\mathbb{H}}(W)$ of one-point conformal blocks over the upper half-plane $\mathbb{H}$ with the trivial bundle of intertwining operators. In particular, bases of intertwining operators give rise to global frames of $\mathscr{C}_{\mathbb{H}}(W)$ via their trace functions. Factorization of conformal-block bundles provides a rank formula used to establish this identification and also yields a geometric proof of basic properties of the fusion ring. Then the modular group $\mathrm{SL}(2,\mathbb Z)$ acts projectively on such a frame, with matrices independent of $\tau \in \mathbb H$. This modular-invariance result recovers that of Zhu for vertex-operator traces and gives a uniform geometric interpretation of the affine and Virasoro intertwining-operator traces studied by Etingof--Kirillov, Krauel--Marks, and Krauel--Shafiq--Wood. The trace frame is horizontal for a natural connection whose projectivization agrees with the pullback of the Damiolini--Gibney--Tarasca connection; after descent, its monodromy gives the modular action. With respect to this natural connection, we characterize global horizontal sections in terms of Miyamoto's four conditions. As an application of our results, we realize the cusp form $\Delta$ as a trace function for the affine VOA $L_{\widehat{\mathfrak{sl}}_2}(16,0)$.
item.dc:creator: Xu Gao, Jianqi Liu

item.title: Deformation quantization of symplectic vector fields
item.description: arXiv:2602.10988v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we study deformation quantization of symplectic vector fields \`a la Fedosov. We provide an explicit construction to quantize each symplectic vector field as a derivation of the deformed star algebra. This recovers a result of M\"uller-Bahns and Neumaier with an explicit formula of higher total degree terms. Moreover, we show that this quantization yields a non-abelian $2$-cocycle on the Lie algebra of symplectic vector fields with values in the deformed star algebra. For a Fedosov deformation quantization with vanishing first characteristic class, this non-abelian $2$-cocycle can provide a formal deformation of the crossed-product algebra generated by the action of symplectic vector fields. In this sense, we can quantize any Lie algebra action by symplectic vector fields.
item.dc:creator: Haoyuan Gao

item.title: Evaluation-type deformed modules over the quantum affine vertex algebras of type $A$
item.description: arXiv:2604.12842v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $\mathcal{V}^c(\mathfrak{gl}_N)$ be Etingof-Kazhdan's quantum affine vertex algebra associated with the trigonometric $R$-matrix. We establish a connection between suitably generalized deformed $\phi$-coordinated $\mathcal{V}^c(\mathfrak{gl}_N)$-modules and the representations of quantized enveloping algebra $U_h(\mathfrak{gl}_N)$ and reflection equation algebra $\mathcal{O}_h(Mat_N)$. As an application, we demonstrate how the elements of the center of $\mathcal{V}^c(\mathfrak{gl}_N)$ at the critical level $c=-N$ give rise to the $q$-analogues of quantum immanants for $U_h(\mathfrak{gl}_N)$, which were recently found by Jing, Liu and Molev. Finally, we derive the analogues of these results for the quantum affine vertex algebra associated with the normalized Yang $R$-matrix.
item.dc:creator: Lucia Bagnoli, Slaven Ko\v{z}i\'c

item.title: Modular fusion categories with trivial Torelli group actions
item.description: arXiv:2608.04462v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we study modular fusion categories whose mapping class group representations are trivial on the Torelli groups, with particular emphasis on the congruence properties of the resulting representations of $\mathrm{Sp}(2g, \mathbb{Z})$. We prove that, for any $g \ge 3$, the Torelli group is contained in the kernel of the genus-$g$ mapping class group representation $\rho_g$ associated with a modular fusion category $\mathcal{C}$ if and only if $\mathcal{C}$ is pointed. This refines the corresponding result in \cite{MW25}. We also characterize the modular fusion categories for which the genus-$2$ Torelli group is contained in $\ker \rho_2$; in particular, categories with isotropic adjoint subcategories belong to this class. Finally, we give a complete classification of modular fusion categories with isotropic adjoint subcategories, and determine the groups $G$ satisfying $\mathcal{Z}(\mathrm{Vect}_G)$ is 2-Torelli trivial but $\mathcal{Z}(\mathrm{Vect}_G)_{\mathrm{ad}}$ is not isotropic are precisely 2-Engel groups of nilpotent class 3.
item.dc:creator: Liang Chang, Siu-Hung Ng, Yilong Wang

item.title: Local Ocneanu rigidity for separable algebra objects
item.description: arXiv:2609.10440v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We establish local Ocneanu rigidity for separable algebra objects in Hom-finite monoidal categories C over an algebraically closed field k. A separability morphism contracts the first two Hochschild cohomology groups without requiring an abelian ambient category. Separable algebra structures and homomorphisms from separable sources have open algebraic-group orbits, and affine Bezout estimates give effective finiteness results. For Frobenius subalgebras, exchange relations replace the source and embedding data by a single self-dual idempotent. We prove that their separable inner-conjugacy classes are open in the exchange locus, yielding a bound of 2^(dim_k(End_C(X))) for any ambient Frobenius algebra X; connectedness gives the same bound on the actual number of subalgebras. As an application, we obtain an effective form of the Etingof-Walton finiteness theorem: every finite-dimensional semisimple Hopf algebra H over C has fewer than 2^(dim_C(H)) left coideal subalgebras. In the unitary setting, we bound E-compatible intermediates of C*-algebra and von Neumann algebra inclusions up to unitary conjugacy, under finite-index and finite-center hypotheses. For irreducible finite-index subfactors N < M, we improve the 9^[M:N] bound of Bakshi-Das-Liu-Ren to fewer than 2^[M:N] intermediate subfactors.
item.dc:creator: Tinhinane Amina Azzouz, Mainak Ghosh, Sebastien Palcoux

item.title: Higher Fomin-Kirillov algebras are infinite-dimensional
item.description: arXiv:2610.10144v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We show that the Fomin--Kirillov algebras $FK_n$ are infinite-dimensional for $n\geq6$. This answers a question posed by Fomin and Kirillov in 1997. To prove this, we demonstrate that the Nichols algebras supported on the conjugacy class of transpositions of the symmetric group are infinite-dimensional for both relevant 2-cocycles. For this, we develop a new method of partially semisimplifying a Nichols algebra along an automorphism of order $p$ in characteristic $p$.
item.dc:creator: N. Andruskiewitsch, I. Angiono, I. Heckenberger, S. Lentner, C. Reiher, L. Vendramin

item.title: Large condensation in enriched $\infty$-categories
item.description: arXiv:2506.23632v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We demonstrate that many algebraic features of higher condensation theory are really features of higher algebra. We work in the context of monads on the unit of a monoidal 2- category. Assuming that 2-categorical unstraightening is monoidal, we show that the functor which takes such a monad to its Eilenberg-Moore object is lax monoidal. We use this to introduce an analog of condensation for codimension-i symmetries, without assuming dualizability. We give sufficient conditions for Morita equivalence of endomorphisms of condensates. We relate higher centralizers to iterated categories of modules. Along the way, we prove results pertaining to functoriality of Day convolution for enriched infinity-categories, which may be of independent interest.
item.dc:creator: Devon Stockall

item.title: On the computation of the canonical basis for irreducible highest weight $U_q (\mathfrak{gl}_{\infty})$-modules
item.description: arXiv:2601.16889v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study canonical basis elements in higher-level Fock spaces associated with the quantum group $U_q(\mathfrak{gl}_\infty)$, which are conjecturally related to Calogero-Moser theory for complex reflection groups. We generalize the Leclerc-Miyachi formula to arbitrary levels by introducing new explicit constructions based on symbols, including a column removal theorem and closed formulas in several cases. These results provide explicit descriptions of canonical basis elements with applications to Calogero-Moser cellular characters and to the decomposition matrices of Ariki-Koike algebras.
item.dc:creator: Nicolas Jacon, Abel Lacabanne

item.title: Hopf $2$-cocycles for certain affine algebraic reductive groups
item.description: arXiv:2607.18599v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $G$ be a reductive affine algebraic group over $\mathbb C$ with toral identity component $T$ and finite component group $K$. We describe finite indecomposable semisimple module categories over $\Rep(G)$ using equivariant data that incorporate the extension class. We prove that every fiber functor is classical and determine the image of its Hopf $2$-cocycle support in $K$ and its intersection with $T$. This yields a minimality criterion involving a finite stabilizer cocycle and an alternating bicharacter on a sublattice of $\widehat T$ of index at most $|K|$. When $\dim T=1$, every Hopf $2$-cocycle for $G$ has finite support of order at most $|K|^2$. We compute all gauge classes for the split and nonsplit extensions with component group $\mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z}$ and inversion action, and compare the support formulas with the K\"unneth coordinates for commutative direct products. Finally, for an arbitrary reductive group $G$, a minimal Hopf $2$-cocycle in a regular deformation of the trivial Hopf $2$-cocycle forces $G$ to be a torus. This uses locality and rigidity of algebraic matrix coefficients on the semisimple quotient of $G$.
item.dc:creator: Shlomo Gelaki

item.title: Integrable multi-species SSEP with reactive particle species
item.description: arXiv:2607.18959v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We investigate integrable exclusion Markov processes constructed from set-theoretical solutions of the Yang-Baxter Equation (YBE) that generalise the multi-species Symmetric Simple Exclusion Process (SSEP). We first introduce the process called the $ (p,1) $-SSEP that is analogous to the multi-species SSEP but with an extra particle species qualified as reactive. Reactive species are able to evaporate and condense by pairs or to transform by pairs depending on the interpretation. We provide a full combinatorial study of the sectors in the periodic case. We prove the integrability of the process in the periodic case and in the open case for two types of boundaries that we introduce using Baxterisations of solutions of the reflection equation. Next we move on to the process called $ (p,q) $-SSEP, i.e. the multi-species SSEP with an arbitrary number of reactive particle species. We prove its integrability in the periodic case and, for the open case, we introduce integrable boundaries generalising the ones considered for the $ (p,1) $-SSEP. Finally, we define physical quantities relevant to the models and we compute them in the non-equilibrium stationary state of the open $ (p,q) $-SSEP for one type of integrable boundaries.
item.dc:creator: Mathieu Dabrowski, Lo\"ic Poulain d'Andecy, Eric Ragoucy

item.title: Leading term strandings for webs
item.description: arXiv:2608.27425v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: A web is a plane graph encoding an invariant vector in a tensor product of fundamental representations of a quantum group. A stranding of an $\mathfrak{sl}_n$ web is a system of colored oriented curves recording one monomial of the vector it encodes. This article focuses on identifying and constructing leading term strandings, those recording the leading term of a web's vector with respect to a lexicographic order on monomials. We show that every open strand of a leading term stranding is clockwise, so the boundary data of such a stranding is recorded by a row-strict tableau. From a row-strict tableau, we construct a web with a prescribed leading term, and the resulting webs form a web basis. This non recursive construction recovers Fontaine's bases and produces others. For $\mathfrak{sl}_3$ webs with no flat vertices, we identify a leading term stranding using the depths of the faces of the web. Finally, we ask whether any two strandings of a web are connected by a sequence of local moves called strand reversals. We answer this question affirmatively for $\mathfrak{sl}_3$, extending a known result for closed webs to webs with boundary; in particular, a leading term stranding of any $\mathfrak{sl}_3$ web is always reachable from an arbitrary stranding.
item.dc:creator: Michael Bo, Madelyn Burns, Junyang Chen, Blaise Marsho, Jacob Martin, Jade Mawn, Bella Mohren, Heather M. Russell, Caitlin Sales, Lance Wong
